name: English Language
description: Grammar, lexis and structure, comprehension and summary, essay writing, oral English and figures of speech for the Nigerian senior secondary curriculum, aligned to WAEC, NECO and JAMB requirements.

topics.name: Parts of Speech
topics.summary: The eight word classes and the job each one does inside a sentence.

subtopics.name: Nouns
subtopics.summary: Naming words, their classes, number, gender and grammatical functions.

objectives.text: Classify nouns as common, proper, abstract, collective or material
Form the plural of regular and irregular nouns correctly
Identify the function of a noun as subject, object or complement

subtopics.name: Pronouns
subtopics.summary: Words that stand in for nouns, and the case and agreement rules that govern them.

objectives.text: Identify personal, reflexive, relative, demonstrative and indefinite pronouns
Choose the correct pronoun case in subject and object positions
Make a pronoun agree with its antecedent in number and person

subtopics.name: Verbs
subtopics.summary: Action, linking and auxiliary verbs, transitivity and the principal parts of a verb.

objectives.text: Distinguish action verbs from linking and auxiliary verbs
Tell transitive verbs apart from intransitive verbs
Use the principal parts of regular and irregular verbs correctly

subtopics.name: Adjectives and Adverbs
subtopics.summary: Modifiers: what each one describes, how they compare and where they belong.

objectives.text: Separate adjectives from adverbs by what each word modifies
Form comparative and superlative degrees correctly
Place modifiers so that the meaning stays clear

subtopics.name: Prepositions and Conjunctions
subtopics.summary: Linking words: prepositional collocations and the joining work of conjunctions.

objectives.text: Select the preposition that a given verb, noun or adjective requires
Use coordinating, subordinating and correlative conjunctions accurately
Correct common Nigerian-English preposition errors

topics.name: Sentence Structure
topics.summary: How phrases and clauses combine to build simple, compound and complex sentences.

subtopics.name: Phrases
subtopics.summary: Groups of words without a finite verb, and the grammatical work each one does.

objectives.text: Define a phrase and distinguish it from a clause
Identify noun, verb, adjectival, adverbial and prepositional phrases
State the function of a named phrase in a sentence

subtopics.name: Clauses
subtopics.summary: Main and subordinate clauses, and the noun, adjectival and adverbial roles they take.

objectives.text: Separate main clauses from subordinate clauses
Classify a subordinate clause as noun, adjectival or adverbial
State the precise function of an underlined clause

subtopics.name: Sentence Types
subtopics.summary: Classifying sentences by structure and by purpose, and repairing faulty ones.

objectives.text: Classify sentences as simple, compound, complex or compound-complex
Classify sentences by function as declarative, interrogative, imperative or exclamatory
Correct sentence fragments and run-on sentences

topics.name: Tenses and Concord
topics.summary: Choosing the right verb form for time, and making subject and verb agree.

subtopics.name: Tenses
subtopics.summary: The twelve tense forms and the time relationships each one signals.

objectives.text: Name the simple, continuous, perfect and perfect continuous forms
Choose the tense that matches a given time expression
Keep tense consistent within a passage and in reported speech

subtopics.name: Subject-Verb Concord
subtopics.summary: The agreement rules examiners test most: proximity, collective nouns and correlatives.

objectives.text: Apply the basic rule that a singular subject takes a singular verb
Handle concord with correlatives, collective nouns and indefinite pronouns
Ignore intervening phrases when locating the true subject

subtopics.name: Active and Passive Voice
subtopics.summary: Turning sentences from active to passive and judging when each voice is better.

objectives.text: Identify whether a sentence is in the active or the passive voice
Change a sentence from active to passive without altering meaning
Explain when the passive voice is the better choice

topics.name: Punctuation and Capitalisation
topics.summary: The marks that make written meaning unambiguous, and the rules for capital letters.

subtopics.name: Punctuation Marks
subtopics.summary: Commas, semicolons, colons, dashes and end stops, and the meaning each carries.

objectives.text: Name the common punctuation marks and state the function of each
Use commas, semicolons and colons in the right places
Explain how a misplaced mark changes the meaning of a sentence

subtopics.name: Capitalisation and Apostrophes
subtopics.summary: When a word takes a capital letter, and how apostrophes show possession or omission.

objectives.text: Apply the rules for capital letters in names, titles and headings
Use the apostrophe for possession in singular and plural nouns
Distinguish contractions from possessive pronouns such as its and whose

topics.name: Vocabulary Development
topics.summary: Building word power through synonyms, antonyms, affixation and fixed expressions.

subtopics.name: Synonyms and Antonyms
subtopics.summary: Choosing the nearest word in meaning, or its opposite, using context.

objectives.text: Select the synonym that fits the context of a sentence
Select the antonym of a word as used in a sentence
Use context clues to judge shades of meaning

subtopics.name: Word Formation
subtopics.summary: Prefixes, suffixes, roots, compounding and conversion as sources of new words.

objectives.text: Explain how prefixes and suffixes change meaning or word class
Derive nouns, adjectives and verbs from a given root word
Recognise compounding, blending, clipping and acronyms

subtopics.name: Idioms and Collocations
subtopics.summary: Fixed expressions whose meaning is not the sum of their words.

objectives.text: Interpret common English idioms in context
Complete a collocation with the word English usage requires
Avoid distorting fixed expressions when writing

topics.name: Comprehension and Summary
topics.summary: Reading a passage accurately and reducing it to its essential points.

subtopics.name: Comprehension Strategies
subtopics.summary: Skimming, scanning, inference, tone and figurative meaning in a passage.

objectives.text: Locate explicitly stated information in a passage
Draw inferences and identify the writer's tone and attitude
Explain the meaning of an expression as used in a passage

subtopics.name: Summary Writing
subtopics.summary: Answering the exact question set, in one sentence, in your own words.

objectives.text: Separate main ideas from illustrations and repetition
Answer a summary rubric in one complete sentence per point
Avoid lifting whole expressions from the passage

topics.name: Essay Writing
topics.summary: Format, register and organisation for the main WAEC and NECO composition tasks.

subtopics.name: Formal Letters
subtopics.summary: The official letter: two addresses, salutation, heading, formal register and subscript.

objectives.text: Lay out the features of a formal letter in the correct order
Match salutation and subscription correctly
Sustain a formal register throughout the letter

subtopics.name: Informal Letters
subtopics.summary: The friendly letter to family or friends: one address and a warm, personal register.

objectives.text: List the features of an informal letter and their order
Contrast informal letter format with formal letter format
Use an appropriately warm but grammatical register

subtopics.name: Article and Speech Writing
subtopics.summary: Writing for a named publication or a named audience, with the right framing devices.

objectives.text: Include the features an article for publication requires
Open and close a speech with appropriate vocatives and courtesies
Adjust content to the stated audience and purpose

subtopics.name: Narrative Essays
subtopics.summary: Telling a story with a clear plot, consistent past tense and sensory detail.

objectives.text: Plan a narrative with orientation, complication and resolution
Maintain a consistent narrative viewpoint and tense
Use descriptive detail and dialogue to hold the reader

subtopics.name: Argumentative and Debate Essays
subtopics.summary: Arguing one side persuasively, refuting the other, and using debate conventions.

objectives.text: Structure an argument with claim, evidence and refutation
Use the vocatives and framing a debate script requires
Choose connectives that signal contrast, addition and conclusion

topics.name: Oral English
topics.summary: Vowel and consonant sounds, word stress, emphatic stress and intonation patterns.

subtopics.name: Vowel Sounds
subtopics.summary: The twelve pure vowels and eight diphthongs of Received Pronunciation.

objectives.text: Distinguish short vowels from long vowels
Group words that share the same vowel sound
Recognise diphthongs and the glide within them

subtopics.name: Consonant Sounds
subtopics.summary: The twenty-four consonants, their voicing, and the clusters Nigerian speakers simplify.

objectives.text: Classify consonants by voicing and manner of articulation
Group words that share the same consonant sound
Identify silent letters and consonant clusters

subtopics.name: Word Stress
subtopics.summary: Which syllable carries the stress, and how stress shifts with word class and suffix.

objectives.text: Locate the stressed syllable in a polysyllabic word
Apply stress shift between noun and verb pairs
Use suffix rules to predict where stress falls

subtopics.name: Intonation and Emphatic Stress
subtopics.summary: Rising and falling tunes, and the stressed word that answers a particular question.

objectives.text: Choose the falling or rising tune a given utterance needs
Identify the word carrying emphatic stress in a sentence
Explain how emphatic stress changes the meaning conveyed

topics.name: Figures of Speech
topics.summary: Literary devices that create effect, and how to name them accurately in an extract.

subtopics.name: Figures of Comparison
subtopics.summary: Simile, metaphor, personification, apostrophe and metonymy.

objectives.text: Distinguish a simile from a metaphor
Identify personification, apostrophe and metonymy in an extract
Explain the effect a comparison creates

subtopics.name: Figures of Sound and Contrast
subtopics.summary: Alliteration, assonance, onomatopoeia, irony, oxymoron, hyperbole and euphemism.

objectives.text: Identify alliteration, assonance and onomatopoeia
Tell irony, paradox and oxymoron apart
Recognise hyperbole, litotes and euphemism

topics.name: Registers and Usage
topics.summary: Matching vocabulary and formality to the field, audience and situation.

subtopics.name: Registers in Context
subtopics.summary: Naming the field a set of specialist words belongs to, from law to agriculture.

objectives.text: Define register and explain why it varies by situation
Match a set of specialist words to its occupational field
Choose the correct register word for a given context

subtopics.name: Formal and Informal Usage
subtopics.summary: Standard English against slang, colloquialism and Nigerian Pidgin.

objectives.text: Grade expressions from formal through colloquial to slang
Rewrite an informal expression in Standard English
Judge which register a stated audience requires

sources.title: WAEC English Language Syllabus — Lexis and Structure, Oral Forms, Comprehension, Summary and Essay
NERDC Senior Secondary English Studies Curriculum
